body_markdown:
Nuevo urbano is a sound—and culture—all its own. With genre-blurring beats and strong sense of community, the scene has gained momentum in recent years, along with a loyal fanbase in its home country of Spain and beyond. Last night, Spotify brought the energy of


[nuevo urbano 2026](https://open.spotify.com/playlist/37i9dQZF1DX8EnL5nCWhbP?si=557a0583d34c43f6) to life at Sala Shôko in Madrid, gathering fans alongside the artists and producers shaping the country’s rising music scene.


“Our editors connect the dots between the trends that are shaping Spanish music today,” said


**Melanie Parejo** , Head of Music Iberia at Spotify. “They look at what fans are gravitating toward, emerging sounds, and their cultural context. That’s how nuevo urbano ended up on our radar. It’s capturing more listener attention every day, while producers, artists, and the wider music community are influencing one another to create a scene that’s greater than the sum of its parts.”


Guests at the event got an in-depth look at the genre with Spotify Iberia Editorial Lead,


**Darío Manrique,** and Spain Editor,


**Mónica Madridejos** , followed by a lively panel featuring Melanie Parejo,


**Nadia Leal** , journalist at


*Neo2* magazine, artists


[Metrika](https://open.spotify.com/artist/51WwqSqhXeyz3q9Q105Kjy?si=4304d738e33143c0) ,


[Kristina](https://open.spotify.com/artist/07Z7bvJe6gxi40UxVpuEL1?si=2962a31593284bd5) , and


[l0rna](https://open.spotify.com/artist/2kFBKRwutklbaGSKBpc6TS?si=0e34ee1f4408445c) , and producer


[Rico Rosa](https://open.spotify.com/artist/33AxM64O965URn5WUtqNST?si=f3527a87d46e4252) . Together, they explored the scene’s evolution and the influences remixing the genre today.


Then it was time to turn up the volume. Kristina,


[C. Marí](https://open.spotify.com/artist/7uthE7Fmy5aYOwlu1Yt4Ps?si=ce542b25d13a416a) ,


[Juicy BAE](https://open.spotify.com/artist/46K14JAfAHpxTSkb6KkFfN?si=e5fe0352da1c49e8) ,


[Xiyo](https://open.spotify.com/artist/2FzRIRtYVDBIJBvTqh7xzQ?si=1d06f0d6bbbf42b6) , and


[Fernandezz](https://open.spotify.com/artist/7mVQGK5j4VKkAvdOhUotB1?si=924624007ae74eaf) hit the stage with performances that got the crowd on its feet.


NEXT


## **Inside nuevo urbano**


Today, the nuevo urbano 2026 playlist racks up 700,000 streams on Spotify every month. That enthusiasm is driving discovery and building dedicated fanbases, with every featured artist seeing year-over-year growth.


Kristina has had a particularly stellar year, growing her audience by over 1,000%.


What makes the genre stand out and resonate? For one, it pulls from a wide range of influences—like reggaeton, trap, and R&B—blending traditional beats with electronic sounds.


Diversity isn’t just found in the tracks that make up the genre. Women artists like Metrika, l0rna, and Kristina are among the nuevo urbano’s biggest hitmakers, while LGBTQIA+ community are helping shape the aesthetics, attitude, and language of the scene.


When it comes to collaboration, nuevo urbano’s got that in spades, too.Take l0rna and Rico Rosa teaming up for “


[MARIMANDONA](https://open.spotify.com/track/6vxRfzTb3I2gzEj1oSgBR5?autoplay_ok=1) ,” or “


[LA SACAPUNTAS](https://open.spotify.com/track/7mjWqfMjappj2v1Iw3rXeR) ,” a powerhouse track that brought together


[Kabasaki](https://open.spotify.com/artist/4rO00pQq33bIv73QyJdivX) ,


[Zeno El Faraón](https://open.spotify.com/artist/1K15TdvUep1VIcFo0B6C1C) , l0rna, and Kristina.


As nuevo urbano reaches new listeners, Spotify will continue supporting the artists defining the genre and bringing fans together, online and off.


*Get to know Spain’s emerging sound through the nuevo urbano 2026 playlist.*
